issues.failure_explanation: Bounding the weighted interior residual of (u_eps,f_eps) by P times the norms of u-u_eps, f-f_eps, and the weighted boundary residual by P times the norm of u_theta-u, requires the weighted residuals to vanish at the exact (u,f). This holds only when the weights coincide (phi_1 = phi_bar_i = phi_2 = phi_3, phi_6 = phi_7, phi_8 = phi_9). For example, with phi_1 = 2 and the other weights equal to 1, the interior residual of (u,f) is d_t u, which is nonzero. With phi_6 differing from phi_7, the initial term at u_theta(0) = u0 is (phi_6 - phi_7)u0. The theorem asserts the bound for any weight parameters, so the proof fails for generic weights.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either restrict to weight tuples for which the exact pair solves the weighted system, or add and control the mismatch terms involving (phi-1) times derivatives of u. The latter needs W^{2,infty}-type bounds on u and a relation between rho and those bounds, and changes the statement.
issues.overall_effect: None of the four forward approximation theorems is established for genuinely non-uniform weights, which is the whole point of WeightedPINN. They hold only in the trivial equal-weights case (essentially standard PINN).
issues.title: Weighted residuals assumed to vanish at the exact state-control pair for arbitrary weights
issues.why_classification: The central guarantee type ('for any weights') fails. Any repair either reduces to standard PINN or changes hypotheses and conclusion substantially.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, let $\omega \subset \Omega$ be an open subset, and let $T>0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited approximation result gives a rate whose exponent involves the input dimension of the approximated function. Here u_eps and f_eps are functions on Q_T, a subset of R^{d+1}, so the exponent should be 2/(d+1), not 2/d. The scaling condition W^{1/d}L^{1/d} >= eps^{-(d+7)/2} and the final rate W^{-1/d}L^{-1/d} are therefore derived from a misapplied result.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the cited result with input dimension d+1, redo the choice of W and L, and restate the rate as W^{-1/(d+1)}L^{-1/(d+1)} (with adjusted constants).
issues.overall_effect: The stated convergence rates in all forward theorems are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Approximation rate uses dimension d for networks on the (d+1)-dimensional space-time domain
issues.why_classification: The fix is mechanical but necessarily worsens the advertised rate. It is a limited weakening that leaves a comparable result.

issues.failure_explanation: The forward theorems bound the loss only for each fixed weight tuple, with constants through P depending on that tuple. Assumption (A2) gives no uniform bound over the weight class. The 'total WeightedPINN loss' is the maximum over weights, which is also the hypothesis of the converse theorems, and that maximum is not controlled. The claimed link between the forward and converse theorems is therefore not established.

failure_location.quote: In particular, the results guarantee that the total WeightedPINN loss can be made arbitrarily small by an appropriate choice of network width and depth.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume a uniform sup bound on the weight class (as in the numerics, outputs in [0.2,5]) and prove the forward bound uniformly over that class (after fixing ISSUE-001). Otherwise restrict the claim to fixed weights.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised convergence chain (small min-max loss attainable, hence convergence of the state and control) is not supported.
issues.title: Fixed-weight bounds do not control the min-max WeightedPINN loss
issues.why_classification: The repair requires an added uniform hypothesis and a uniform version of the estimate, not a new architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: that the above semilinear heat equation admits a unique solution

issues.failure_explanation: The forward parabolic equation with a terminal condition is the backward heat problem, which is ill-posed: in general there is no solution for z0 in L^2, and there is no continuous dependence. Integrating the inequality d_t||u_hat||^2 + ||u_hat||_{H^1}^2 <= C0(...) from t to T yields a lower bound on ||u_hat(t)||^2, not the claimed upper bound in terms of ||u_hat(T)||^2. Estimate (eq:hat_u_est1) is therefore unfounded.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must rebuild the argument with a forward-in-time comparison problem (initial data u0) and a separate mechanism to relate terminal mismatch to the control error.
issues.overall_effect: The converse error estimate for the heat equation is unproven, so convergence of trained networks to the state and control is not supported.
issues.title: Heat stability argument uses an ill-posed backward heat problem and a reversed Gronwall inequality
issues.why_classification: The proof architecture must be replaced; no backward parabolic stability estimate of this form exists.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \(f-f_{\bar{\theta}}\) is the exact control with corresponding weak solution \(\tilde u\) of the equation
The controllability estimate of \cite[Theorem 4.1]{zuazua2024exactcontrollabilitystabilizationwave} yields a constant

issues.failure_explanation: Controllability results assert the existence of some control with norm at most C times the data. They do not bound every control steering the data to zero. Controls are non-unique: e.g. for v=0, take psi in C_c^infty(q_T) nonzero; then (u+psi, f+(d_t - Delta)psi) solves the same control problem with the same initial and terminal data. Networks approximating it have arbitrarily small loss, yet ||f - f_theta|| stays near ||(d_t - Delta)psi||. The same counterexample works for the wave equation with d_tt. Thus the stated conclusions are false for a prescribed control f.

failure_location.quote: The controllability estimate of \cite[Theorem 1.6]{fernandez-cara_guerrero_2006} yields a constant

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must single out a unique control (e.g. a minimal-norm or HUM-type selection, enforced in the loss) and prove stability for that selection.
issues.overall_effect: Both converse theorems fail as stated: small loss does not imply proximity to a given control or state.
issues.title: Controllability cost estimate misused as a bound on an arbitrary control (controls are non-unique)
issues.why_classification: The central conclusion is false by counterexample. Recovery requires changing the problem formulation and the proof.

issues.failure_explanation: The H^1 norm on the boundary manifold contains only tangential derivatives, so ||grad u_theta . nu||_{L^2(boundary)} is not bounded by ||u_theta||_{H^1(boundary)}. A function vanishing on the boundary with nonzero normal derivative is a counterexample. If instead the norm means the full gradient on Sigma_T (as the 2D weighted residual suggests), the exact solution generally has a nonzero normal derivative. Its boundary residual is then nonzero, and the forward trace step comparing with u fails. Either way the argument breaks. The wave proof uses the same bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Handle the Dirichlet mismatch by a lifting or transposition argument with appropriate boundary norms (e.g. H^{1/2}/H^{3/2} traces), adjusting the boundary penalty accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The energy estimates handling non-zero boundary traces of u_theta are unsupported.
issues.title: Normal derivative on the boundary is not controlled by the boundary residual
issues.why_classification: Requires a contained replacement argument for nonhomogeneous Dirichlet data, but no new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: is the closed ball centered at $(1/d,\dots,1/d)$ with radius $3/4$
For simplicity, we further assume that $\omega$ contains the entire boundary $\partial\Omega$.

issues.failure_explanation: For d=10 the center c has |c| = 1/sqrt(10), about 0.316. The boundary point c/|c| lies at distance about 0.684 < 3/4 from c, so the removed closed ball meets the unit sphere. Hence that ball is not contained in Omega, and omega contains neither a neighbourhood of the boundary nor the whole boundary. The claim that (A3) holds is false.
